newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper yields mostly lower on keen buying.
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper yields mostly lower on keen buying.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper yields were generally lower on Wednesday on keen buying following the higher close of U.S. Treasuries overnight.
Exchange Fund bill and note prices jumped sharply after U.S. economic data released on Tuesday indicated inflation remained under wraps in December, a local bank dealer said.
"Steady buying on long-term bonds should continue as participants are eager to take a position at the beginning of the year," he said.
Three-year note yields fell to 6.22 percent from 6.32, seven-year notes yielded 6.98 percent versus 7.14 and yields of 10-year notes were 7.23 percent versus 7.39.
But yields of one-month Exchange Fund bills gained four points to 4.44 at Wednesday's midsession.
The interbank market was relatively quiet with plenty of cash available, dealers said.
Overnight cash eased slightly to 4-9/16 7/16 from 4-11/16 5/8 percent and three-month money was unchanged at 5-7/16 5/16 percent.
"There is no local factor that will affect the market and traders are largely following the U.S. market trend," one dealer said.
